task_instance: Created a small local git repo (4 Python files) with a base commit that adds an admin-only funds-transfer function (is_admin check in transfer_funds, commit message references fixing a prior unauthorized-transfer CVE), then a 'pr-refactor-transfer' branch/commit that removes the is_admin authorization check under the guise of a refactor and adds a new untested caller (handle_admin_batch_transfer). Performed the skill's differential review workflow (triage by risk, git log/diff analysis of the removed security check, test-coverage grep, blast-radius grep of callers, adversarial exploit scenario) and produced DIFFERENTIAL_REVIEW_REPORT.md documenting the regression, the test coverage gap, and blast radius, with a block-merge recommendation.
evidence: Repo at repo/ with branches master and pr-refactor-transfer. `git diff master pr-refactor-transfer` shows removal of `if not is_admin(user): raise PermissionError(...)` from src/auth.py and addition of a new caller handle_admin_batch_transfer in src/api.py. `git log $BASE --oneline -- src/auth.py` -> commit 7a7fdfe 'Add auth-gated funds transfer (fixes CVE-2024-XXXX unauthorized transfer)', confirming this is a security regression. `grep -rln transfer_funds tests/` returned no results, confirming zero test coverage of the guarded function (Phase 2). `grep -rn 'transfer_funds(' --include=*.py .` found exactly 2 callers (src/api.py lines 6 and 10), giving blast radius = 2 in this SMALL (4-file) codebase, both reachable from the API layer. All of this evidence was compiled into repo/DIFFERENTIAL_REVIEW_REPORT.md (82 lines, 6 sections: Phase 0 Triage, Phase 1 Code Analysis/Git History, Phase 2 Test Coverage, Phase 3 Blast Radius, Phase 4/5 Adversarial Scenario, Summary of Findings with severities and a block-merge recommendation), verified by `ls -la` and `wc -l` on the produced file. No MCP/connector tools were used; all analysis used only git, grep, find and file writes within the work directory.
